full_judgment:
The present opposite party Nos. 1-6 as preemptors filed a preemption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for preempt the case land measuring an area of 5 decimals of land so described to the schedule of the petition for preemption. In the said case the present petitioner as preemptee-purchaser entered its appearance and in order to contest the case also filed written objection. When the said case reached at the stage of further hearing, the preemptor did not turn up resulting in, the learned senior Assistant judge, Jessore dismissed the said case for default on 7-6-2007. 

 4. Challenging the said order of dismissal, the preemptors then filed a Miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 15-07-2007 being Miscellaneous case No. 38 of 2007. After filing of the Miscellaneous case, the preemptee-purchaser on 31-5-2015 filed an application for rejecting the said Miscellaneous case claiming that, the said Miscellaneous case filed under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable in view of the provision of section 96(15) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. However, the application filed for dismissal of the Miscellaneous case was taken up for hearing by the learned Assistant judge, Keshobpur, Jessore on 14-6-2015 and after hearing the parties to the Miscellaneous case, the learned judge rejected the said petition so filed by the preeemptee-purchaser fixing the original preemption case 8-7-2015 for further hearing. Challenging the said judgment and order, the preemptee then filed a civil revision being civil revision No. 15 of 2015 before the learned District judge, Jessore. The said revision was on transfer heard by the learned Additional District judge, 3rd court, Jessore. In the revision, the preemptor also entered his appearance as opposite party and after hearing the parties to the revision, the learned Additional District judge dismissed the revision and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant judge who rejected the application on 14-6-2015. 

 5. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said concurrent judgment and order, the preemptee-purchaser then came before this court and obtained the instant rule and order of stay as stated herein above. 

 6. Mr ABM Golam Mostofa, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner upon taking me to the revisioal application in particular, the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial and that of revisional court below at the very out set submits that, both the courts below has committed an error of law in rejecting the application so filed by the preemptee without considering the express provision so enshrined in sub section 15 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, as the said provision has clearly provided for preferring appeal against any order passed in a preemption case so resorting to the provision of Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure after dismissal of a preemption case cannot be entertained. 

 7. The learned counsel further contends that, though a preemption proceeding is of a civil nature but since there has been specific provision for preferring appeal so a miscellaneous case filed against an order of dismissal for default cannot lie. Giving reference to the provision of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned counsel further submits that, though that very provision has been made applicable in all the proceeding in any court of civil jurisdiction, but since, there has been specific provision in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in particular since section 96 is a special law, so taking recourse to the Code of Civil Procedure in view of having provision of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure is totally misconceived one. With regard to the decision so have been cited by the learned counsel for the opposite party reported in 49 DLR (AD) 212, the learned counsel further submits that, the said decision is not applicable with the facts and circumstances of the instant case and thus prays for making the rule absolute. 

 8. On the contrary, Mr Mohammad Abul Kashem Bhuiyan, the learned counsel appearing for the preemptor-opposite party Nos. 1-6 vehemently opposes the contention so have been placed by the learned counsel for the petitioner and contends that, only point involved in the instant rule is whether the provision of section 96(15) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act will be made applicable or not and whether in case of dismissal of any preemption case for default, Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure will be made applicable. The learned counsel in support of his such submission has also placed his reliance on two decisions reported in 59 DLR (AD) 212 where a decision was referred reported in 57 DLR 143. By drawing my attention to paragraph No. 4 of the Appellate Division's decision as well as paragraph No. 12 of the High Court's Division decision, the learned counsel then contends that similar question was raised in those cited decisions, and their lordships eventually came to a finding that, in case of dismissal of any preemption case for default the provision of Order 9 rule 9 will be applicable. With such submission and relying on those two decisions, the learned counsel finally prays discharging the rule. 

 9. I have considered the submission so advanced by the learned counsel for the contending parties at length and also perused the provision so enunciated in section 96(15) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, as well as the decision cited by the learned counsel for the opposite parties. There has been no gainsaying of facts that, the case was dismissed for default and that of filing the Miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the preemptor as well as the application filed by the preemptee-petitioner for dismissal of the said miscellaneous case (under Order IX, rule9). Only question remains, whether the provision of section 96(15) will be applied in challenging the order of dismissal for default of a preemption Miscellaneous case, where there has been provision to prefer appeal. But by the time, our Honb'le Appellate Division came to a decision that in such a situation there would have no bar to invoke the provision of Order IX, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside any dismissal order for default. Since similar provision has been laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure in case of dismissing a title suit for default so that very provision will equally applicable in a preemption proceeding. The submission so have been advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner that since there has been a clear provision of preferring appeal which is mandatory one so there cannot be any reason to file a Miscellaneous case. But since in the meantime our Honb'le Appellate Division has settled the said point, so this court has got no authority to go beyond the said settled provision of law which is binding upon this court under article 111 of the Constitution.
